business_webhooks.title: Webhooks
business_webhooks.intro: Receive an HTTP POST when a key event happens in your business (shipment created, status changed, quote accepted, etc.) — no need to poll the API.
business_webhooks.hmac_body: Every delivery carries an X-Webhook-Signature header. Recompute server-side: sha256_hmac(secret, timestamp + "." + body). Reject if it doesn't match or the timestamp is stale (> 5 min).
business_webhooks.rotate_confirm: Rotate the secret? The old one stops working immediately.
business_webhooks.delete_confirm: Delete this endpoint? It will stop receiving events.
business_webhooks.reveal_body: This is the only time the secret is shown. Use it server-side to verify the HMAC signature of each delivery.
business_webhooks.retry_hint: Automatic retries with exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 min), up to 6 attempts. After that, the event is marked as failed.

api_docs.meta_description: Pedagogical guide to using the Luna Tracking API: first request in 3 minutes, authentication, endpoints, cURL examples, error handling.
api_docs.hero_intro: Everything you need to plug your tools into Luna Tracking — explained plainly, with concrete examples.
api_docs.what_p1: An API is a door Luna Tracking opens to your tools (website, Excel script, ERP, mobile app…). Instead of retyping your shipments by hand, your tool asks Luna a question in HTTP and gets the answer back as JSON.
api_docs.what_p2: Nothing to install on our servers, no VPN, no gateway — just URLs like any website, except they return data instead of pages.
api_docs.what_analogy_body: The client (your tool) is you at the table. The waiter (the API) takes your order, checks you're allowed to order, and fetches the dish from the kitchen (the database). You never see the kitchen — and that's a good thing.
api_docs.today_intro: The API is already live. These use cases work out of the box:
api_docs.today_c1_b: Fetch the shipment list for a business — reference, status, route — perfect for an internal dashboard.
api_docs.today_c2_b: Full detail by ID: packages, tracking, dates, consignee.
api_docs.today_c3_b: Your B2B address book, exportable in one request.
api_docs.today_c4_b: Currency + weight + volume → available modes and customer prices, no account required.
api_docs.quick_intro: Goal: receive a real response from the API in under 3 minutes. Open a terminal (or an online one like reqbin.com).
api_docs.quick_s1_title: Check the API is up (no account needed)
api_docs.quick_s1_body: Copy the command below and run it. It hits a public endpoint that replies "ok" — like ringing the bell to see who's home.
api_docs.quick_s1_expect: Expected response (the time field will differ):
api_docs.quick_s1_check_body: If you got that JSON, the API is reachable from your machine. Otherwise: check your connection and re-copy the command carefully.
api_docs.quick_s2_body: Endpoints that touch YOUR data need a key. Here's how:
api_docs.quick_s2_l1: Sign up on Luna Tracking and pick "Professional" during onboarding.
api_docs.quick_s2_l4: Click "New key", give it a name, tick the permissions, generate.
api_docs.quick_s2_warn_title: Heads up: the key is shown ONCE
api_docs.quick_s2_warn_body: On generation, copy the full key immediately and store it in a password manager. If you lose it: revoke it and create a new one. We cannot show it to you again.
api_docs.quick_s3_body: Replace YOUR_BUSINESS_ID with your business ID (visible on the dashboard) and lk_live_xxx.YOUR_SECRET with your actual key.
api_docs.auth_title: 4. How you prove who you are
api_docs.auth_intro: The API accepts two ways to authenticate: one for your app (Bearer JWT), one for scripts and integrations (ApiKey). Each request carries the token in the Authorization header; the API verifies it, then answers or refuses.
api_docs.auth_bearer_body: Generated when a human signs in. Great for web/mobile apps where a user drives the request. Expires in one hour and auto-refreshes client-side.
api_docs.auth_apikey_body: A long-lived key, tied to YOUR business only. Never expires but can be revoked at any moment. The right choice for a cron, an ERP, a webhook, a nightly export.
api_docs.auth_never_title: Never in the browser, never in Git
api_docs.auth_never_body: An ApiKey grants access to YOUR business data. Never put it in browser JavaScript, don't commit it to GitHub, don't email it. Use a secret manager (1Password, Vault, env variables).
api_docs.resp_intro: Every response has the same shape: either { data } (with optional { meta }), or { error } with a code and a message. Write your code once, reuse everywhere.
api_docs.resp_header_body: Each response carries an X-Api-Version header. Check it client-side to be sure you're talking to the right version:
api_docs.ep_intro: Two groups: public (no auth), and business-scoped (Bearer JWT or ApiKey).
api_docs.ep_root: Discovery: lists every endpoint with its signature.
api_docs.ep_rates: Rate calculator: returns available modes and customer prices — internal cost is never exposed.
api_docs.ep_tracking: Public shipment tracking by token (the shipper toggles sharing from their dashboard).
api_docs.ep_me: Caller profile: user id + businesses + roles.
api_docs.ep_ship_list: Shipment list for the business (JWT or scoped ApiKey). Filters: status, limit.
api_docs.ep_ship_get: Full shipment detail. RLS + ApiKey scope enforced.
api_docs.ep_usage: Aggregated usage: totals + timeline + top endpoints + per-key breakdown, over the requested window.
api_docs.ep_perms_body: When you create a key, you pick what it can do. A minimal tick list keeps the blast radius small if the key leaks.
api_docs.oa_intro: The API is described in OpenAPI 3.1 — the standard machine-readable format. Import it directly into Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, Swagger Editor, or any SDK generator. The file is served live from our server: every new API version reflects automatically.
api_docs.oa_import_body: Click a tool below — the spec URL is preloaded, the viewer fills itself in.
api_docs.oa_postman_note: Copy the URL above, then Postman → Import → Link.
api_docs.oa_sdk_title: Generate an SDK in your language
api_docs.oa_sdk_body: The spec is enough to generate a typed client (TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, Rust, PHP, C#…). Two examples:
api_docs.err_intro: Errors always look like { error: { code, message } }. Code the field, not the message (which may be translated).
api_docs.err_missing_param: A required parameter is missing (e.g. business_id).
api_docs.err_bad_id: An ID is not a valid UUID.
api_docs.err_unauth: No token, or an expired / invalid token.
api_docs.err_forbid: Token is valid but lacks access to this resource (wrong business, missing permission).
api_docs.err_not_found: The requested object does not exist, or the tracking link is not enabled.
api_docs.err_internal: Unexpected error inside the API. Contact us with the exact time.
api_docs.limits_intro: The API is currently free. Every call is logged (method, path, status, response time) so we can one day propose fair plans — but no paywall today.
api_docs.limits_free_body: No strict rate limit for now. If you plan thousands of requests per hour, tell us first — we prefer being warned rather than seeing you blocked. A paid tier (Free / Pro / Business / Enterprise) will be announced if volume warrants it — existing customers will get at least 30 days' notice.
api_docs.roadmap_intro: The next chantiers, in order. We won't paywall the API until these bricks are ready.
api_docs.roadmap_i1: Write endpoints (POST /shipments, POST /quotes) — create and update from your tools.
api_docs.roadmap_i2: Webhooks — receive an automatic ping when a status changes (shipment.in_transit, quote.accepted…).
api_docs.roadmap_i3: OpenAPI/Swagger documentation — auto-generate SDKs in your favourite language.
api_docs.roadmap_i4: Official SDKs (JS/Python) — no more cURL to type.
api_docs.cta_body: Sign up, generate a key, make your first request. We reply within 24h if you get stuck.
